title: Adaptive rigorous hR completion
objective: Use a coarse-first exact zeta error schedule for rigorous hR integer-index decisions, refine only when inconclusive, and bind the authenticated history into live and detached certificates while preserving exact class/unit results

C4 quintic [1,4,-1,1,0,1] and quartic x^4-x-1 exact public outputs

handoff.summary: Completed and independently reviewed adaptive rigorous hR completion. The exact zeta error starts at 1 and halves only while the rigorous positive-integer index decision is inconclusive; the selected error and entire decision history are bound into live and detached certificates. Proof-relevant zeta/regulator cache state is owner- and field-bound, altered cache values fail closed, replay applies fixed verifier caps and cancellation, and the immediate standard-engine certificate path reuses an identity- and parameter-bound regulator receipt without weakening detached replay. Focused coverage includes near-boundary refinement, empty-integer refinement, cancellation and caps, cache alteration and cross-workspace rejection, malformed payloads, detached replay, and exact C4/quartic outputs. Independent immutable review returned SAFE. On final source, matched three-sample cold medians improved C4 from 2.5976 s to 2.3052 s (11.25%) and quartic from 1.4693 s to 1.2907 s (12.15%); the C4 analytic phase improved from 0.5824 s to 0.2160 s. Matched prepared-field C4 medians were 0.9090 s at the base and 0.9315 s here, a 2.47% regression within the 5% gate. The final build, strict Python, architecture checks, focused compiled proof tests, slow exact-output witness, and complete native gate passed at 2e91bf5e.
risks: Performance receipts are Linux x64 measurements on a shared host; the required non-Linux platform matrix remains integration/CI work.
next_steps: Integrate the reviewed commit sequence into class-group and retain the cold and prepared-field benchmarks as Amdahl gates while profiling the next exact relation/unit bottleneck.
